grade_rationale.text: Every verified peoples row is Russians: Ralston sets the many-headed Zmei Goruinuich in Russian story-land.
Ralston's passage naming the Snake Zmei Goruinuich does not cite or quote Afanasyev; its one Afanasyev footnote belongs to the Ivan Popyalof story that follows.

Ralston's 1872 passage on the Serpent with the patronymic Goruinuich likewise does not draw on Afanasyev for the clauses used; its Afanasyev footnote attaches only to the Luna and Zvyezda story, not used here.
Afanasyev separately records the Gorynchishche in the Dobrynya bylina and the cave serpent of the Yegory verse, which he equates with Gorynych.
Afanasyev's volumes count as one source and Ralston's two books as another: two independent authors for one people, so the grade is regional.
